Apertix AI's released Cerno 9B v1.2 (apertixai/cerno-9b-v1.2 at f02a632), a full fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B with block-bidirectional attention. Its card ships no server, only an in-process engine (CernoEngine, transformers, BF16); it ran on our hardware, one request at a time, through a thin System One wrapper around that engine, text only: its English runs on one DGX Spark (logic's wrapper), its Turkish runs on one RTX PRO 6000 (compactor's di_serve.py, 15 November 2026). Input tokens are counted only where the engine reports them. Probabilities rounded to 4 decimals by its own code; they sum to 1 only within that rounding.

Latency: the time from sending one request to receiving its answer, measured from our computer, network and any retries within the request included. Request time: the time at least one request was in flight, over the requests whose answers were kept. It is not the run's elapsed time: it leaves out requests that failed and any pause before a run was resumed.

Estimated from GPU time: the run's request time x the GPUs its server held x Runpod's on-demand price for an RTX PRO 6000, $2.49 per GPU-hour (read 5 November 2026). A cloud-equivalent estimate, not measured spending.
